EN: The Launchpad is where vessels built at the VAB start their flights. We are reasonably confident it's at a \nsafe enough distance from everything else.
It is primarily designed for vertical launches, but don't let that stop you from trying variations.
Level 1: 20.0 x 21.2m - 18.0t\nLevel 2: 36.0 x 39.6m - 140.0t\nLevel 3: Unlimited
The Launchpad
At the Mission Control facility, all available contracts can be managed. It also offers a very nice view of \nthe launch sites, for any brave enough to be so close to a launching vessel.
Level 1: 2 active contracts, flight planning unavailable\nLevel 2: 7 active contracts and flight planning\nLevel 3: Unlimited active contracts and flight planning
You can pick and choose the next goals for your space program, and check out the prospective rewards.
Mission Control (MC)
Level 1: 100 Science point limit and no surface samples or resource transfer Level 2: 500 Science point limit, surface samples and resource transfer allowed Level 3: Unlimited science points
At the R&D facility, the team of scientists works hard to crunch the data received from mission \nexperiments. Here, all researched technologies can be viewed, and new ones researched.
You can also review your experimentation history in the archives -- if you're feeling nostalgic.
Research and Development (R&D)
At the Runway, craft built in the SPH have a long flat surface to reach take-off speed. Conceivably, such \naircraft could even land back on it...
The 2.5km length is sufficent for a range of designs and sizes, making it the perfect place for all kinds \nof tests.
Level 1: 20.0 x 15.0m - 18.0t\nLevel 2: 36.0 x 28.0m - 140.0t\nLevel 3: Unlimited
The Runway
This facility is similar to the VAB, both being used for construction. The primary difference being the SPH \nis designed for building horizontally launched craft, that then use the attached Runway.
Level 1: 30 parts and no action groups\nLevel 2: 255 parts and basic action groups\nLevel 3: Unlimited parts and all action groups
It is from here that many planes have been designed to investigate the home planet.
The Spaceplane Hangar (SPH)
Level 1: Orbits in map and flight planning (with upgraded MC)\nLevel 2: Patched conics visible in map\nLevel 3: Patched conics in map and unknown object tracking
At the Tracking Station, all ongoing missions can be viewed and flown. Landed craft can be recovered \nfrom here as well.
It's a great place to get an overall view of your space program and who is out exploring.
The Tracking Station (TS)
The Vehicle Assembly Building (or VAB to those in the know) is the place where rockets and other \nvertically launched spacecraft are designed.
<color=#ef2929>Note: </color>Ignition of rocket engines inside the VAB voids the KSC insurance policy.
From here they are moved over to the launchpad for liftoff.
